subject: GPU pool soft-lock: interim compensation & migration checklist
messages:
From: GlyphTech Ops <ops@glyphtech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Liao <sara.liao@glyphtech.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:12:04 -0700
Subject: High queue depth / 503 spikes on glyphtech-prod-2 dedicated pool

Jonas / Redwood team,

We started seeing sustained queue depth (~90%) on our dedicated pool `glyphtech-prod-2` around 08:45 PT. The result is intermittent 503s on our low-latency endpoints which are customer-facing. We've attached a short log extract below and can share longer traces if needed.

Impact: customer-facing errors for ~10% of traffic, spikes last 5–15 minutes but are recurring every ~30 minutes.

Can you confirm whether this is a routing/fallback issue or something inside the dedicated pool? We need an ETA on resolution and whether you can provide credits for impacted requests while we triage.

Short log excerpt:
[2028-03-27T08:46:11Z] pool=glyphtech-prod-2 queue_len=173 running=12 pending=161 -> 503 on route /v1/generate-low-latency
[2028-03-27T08:51:36Z] pool=glyphtech-prod-2 queue_len=182 running=13 pending=169 -> 503

Thanks,
Sara Liao
Ops Lead, GlyphTech

Attachments: incident-sample.log (text, 45KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: GlyphTech Ops <ops@glyphtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:29:47 -07:00
Subject: Re: High queue depth / 503 spikes on glyphtech-prod-2 dedicated pool

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm escalating this to infra and product; ticket INC-20280327-5226 is opened. Immediate notes and mitigation steps we're applying now: 

- Enabled automated fallback routing for low-latency routes to your warm-standby variant for the next 2 hours to reduce failed requests (we'll monitor error-rate).
- Temporarily increased burst allowance on glyphtech-prod-2 by 25% to buy headroom while we investigate allocation behavior.
- Infra is collecting memory/kernel level counters from the affected nodes.

We're treating this as high priority — I've looped in Marissa (platform ops lead) and Karthik (dedicated infra). I'll update within 45 minutes with any timeline or additional mitigations. If you can share a longer trace or routes affected that would be helpful.

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

--

Subject: Re: High queue depth / 503 spikes on glyphtech-prod-2 dedicated pool

Thanks Jonas.

The fallback reduced immediate errors but we're still seeing brief 503s on critical routes during the spikes. Our execs want to understand exposure and whether Redwood will provide credit for the impacted window — the incidents have hit our premium customers. Please include any timeline for RCA and the scope of credits you can commit to.

Also request: can you provide a short migration checklist if we decide to move the hottest routes to a different pool or region? We want to assess the work.

Sara

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: GlyphTech Ops <ops@glyphtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 17:03:12 -07:00
Subject: GPU pool soft-lock: interim compensation & migration checklist

Sara / GlyphTech team — final update and next steps. Apologies again for the impact here and thank you for your patience while we completed our investigation. Summary below with actions we're committing to and a migration checklist attached.

Summary (high level)
- Root cause: a rare race in the dedicated autoscaler preemption path triggered a soft-lock when multiple long-lived allocation requests coincided with memory fragmentation on two nodes. The soft-lock prevented the allocator from reclaiming KV cache memory, which escalated queue length and resulted in transient 503s during peak bursts.
- Scope: incidents occurred on pool `glyphtech-prod-2` between 2028-03-27T08:44 and 2028-03-27T11:10 PT with recurring spikes; total impacted request volume ~1.1M tokens across affected routes.

Actions taken
- Immediate mitigations (applied 2028-03-27): fallback routing, burst increase, node-level restarts for most-affected instances.
- Hotfix deployed (2028-03-28): allocator race guard and improved memory reclamation heuristics to prevent soft-locks under the observed allocation pattern.
- Ongoing: infra will run a 72-hour soak with synthetic workloads that reproduce the burst pattern; we'll provide the soak results and raw traces.

Customer commitments
- Credits: Redwood will apply a billing credit equal to 25% of the billed usage for the impacted day (2028-03-27) for the `glyphtech-prod-2` pool. Our billing team will apply this as a line-item credit within 7 business days.
- Operational: we will provide a 1-hr technical runbook review and migration planning session at no cost.

Attached: migration-checklist.pdf (5 pages) — short checklist for moving hot routes to another pool/region with recommended config toggles; incident-timeline.csv — detailed event timeline and node IDs.

Migration checklist (excerpt)
- Identify hot routes (top 10 by RPS) and their session/seq length distributions.
- Provision target pool with >=20% headroom and matching quantization profile.
- Warm up KV caches with a synthetic prefix replay at T-60min.
- Verify fallback routing and health probes before cutover.
- Rollback plan: immediate revert to original pool with traffic-split 90/10 for 15 minutes.

Next steps
- I'll schedule the runbook review (Janitor slot) for early next week — suggest Mon/Tue; please send a preferred time.
- We'll share soak data and the full RCA doc within 72 hours.

If you'd like an exec-level summary or to escalate credits beyond the committed amount, loop in your account exec and we'll handle it directly. We're sorry for the disruption and appreciate the quick collaboration to stabilize traffic.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
